hero.headline: No borders. Only bridges.
hero.subhead: Kimere is young, deliberately small, and spread across several countries. We are a network of independent professionals rather than an office with a reception desk — built that way on purpose, because the students and universities we work for are not in one place either. We started in June 2026, we back people early in their careers, and we would rather show you how the work runs than tell you how long we have been doing it.

match.heading: The person on your call comes from where you come from
match.body: Paperwork is only half of what makes moving abroad frightening. The other half is explaining yourself in a language you are still learning, to someone who has never had to do what you are about to do. So we do the obvious thing that almost nobody does: where our team covers your country, that is who takes your call — a Brazilian consultant for a university in Brazil, and the same logic everywhere else we reach.

points.title: Nothing to translate, nothing to explain
points.body: You describe your situation once, in the language you actually think in, to someone who already knows what a diploma from your country looks like and how your school system grades it.

points.title: Universities take the meeting
points.body: An international office is far more willing to sit down with someone who understands their market, their calendar and what their students can genuinely afford — in their own language, without an interpreter in the middle.

points.title: The cultural shorthand does the heavy lifting
points.body: Knowing why a family hesitates, what a parent will ask before they say yes, which reassurance actually lands: none of that is on a checklist, and it saves entire conversations.

match.honestNote: Where we do not yet cover your country, we tell you on the first call and you get the consultant with the closest experience instead. We would rather be one honest sentence short than promise a nationality we cannot actually field.

network.heading: A network, not a head office
network.body: There is no headquarters with a waiting room. Kimere is a coordinated group of independent professionals — each running their own practice, each in their own country, each covering one part of the route. That structure is the reason we can work towards whichever destination a student picks rather than only the one we happen to sit in, and the reason there is usually someone awake when you write.

points.title: Independent professionals, not employees
points.body: Everyone here runs their own practice and carries their own VAT registration. It keeps the team senior and the structure light, and it means you are dealing with people who chose this work rather than people assigned to your file.

points.title: Spread across several countries
points.body: It is what makes the cultural match above possible at all, and what lets us cover a destination without first opening an office in it. Growth here means one more professional in one more country, not one more floor.

points.title: One coordinator, accountable for all of it
points.body: A network could easily turn into pass-the-parcel. It does not, because one named person owns your file from the first call to the last signature, and is the only person you ever have to chase.

team.heading: The people you'll actually deal with
team.body: A small group, deliberately. From the introductory call onwards you have one point of contact, and the others are people that contact can reach in an afternoon — not a ticket queue.

languages.heading: Seven languages beyond Italian — and the same people handle your paperwork
languages.body: Our language teachers are part of the team, not a supplier we call when something needs translating. They run the courses, and they handle the translation of your academic documents. That is not an accident of the org chart: it is the reason a translation can start the day you ask for it, instead of going out to a third party and coming back in three weeks.

inHouse.title: Translation, on our side of the table
inHouse.body: Transcripts, diplomas, certificates — translated by people who are already on your file and already know what the receiving office expects to see, in the format it expects to see it.

inHouse.title: The legalisation file, followed through
inHouse.body: Apostille or consular legalisation depending on the country that issued your qualification, prepared and tracked alongside you rather than handed back to you as a list of instructions.

inHouse.title: Courses built around a student's week
inHouse.body: Freelance teachers, online, scheduled around lectures and exams rather than around an office's opening hours. Start before you leave, keep going once you have landed.

languages.limitBody: It does not mean the requirement disappears. The comparability statement for a foreign qualification is issued by CIMEA or assessed by the university itself, and nothing we do replaces it or makes it optional — anyone telling you the step can be skipped is selling you a rejected application. What we do is build the file, follow it through, and keep the translation on our side so that part is never the one holding you up.

connected.heading: You will hear from us more often than you expect
connected.body: The way this team runs internally is the way it runs with you: frequent alignment calls, a fluid exchange instead of formal handovers, and the client kept inside the process rather than updated about it afterwards. It sounds like a small thing. On a route this long it is most of what makes it bearable.

points.title: Alignment calls, not status reports
points.body: Short, regular, and with the person actually doing the work. You will always know which deadline is next and whose court the ball is currently in.

points.title: A fluid exchange inside the team
points.body: Your coordinator can reach the specialist who handles your consulate in an afternoon. There is no queue between them, because there is no ticketing system to queue in.

points.title: You are involved, not managed
points.body: We ask you to decide the things that are genuinely yours to decide, and we do not arrive with a finished plan you had no part in building.

limits.heading: What we don't do
items: We don't issue visas or residence permits, and we don't guarantee outcomes. Those decisions belong to the consulate and the Questura alone.
We're not accredited by, affiliated with, or acting on behalf of any university or public body — in Italy or anywhere else.
We're not a licensed estate agency. We view, verify and register housing; we don't hold listings or take deposits on anyone's behalf.
We don't replace a lawyer or an accountant. Where a case needs one we say so instead of improvising.
We began operating in June 2026 and the legal structure is being formalised. We share current company documentation directly at the due-diligence stage rather than describe it here.
